items.title: CVE-2026-90561 (CRITICAL 9.3): Strapi versions 4.x through 4.26.2 and 5.x before 5.48.1 contain a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-90561 allows Author-role users to trigger stored XSS leading to account takeover in Strapi versions 4.x and 5.x.
items.summary: Strapi versions 4.x through 4.26.2 and 5.x prior to 5.48.1 contain a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the content manager WYSIWYG preview component due to its failure to properly strip script tags from rich text input. An attacker possessing an Author-role account can insert malicious scripts into rich text fields that execute automatically within the session of an Editor or Super Admin when the preview pane is expanded, potentially leading to account takeover. The vulnerability has been assigned a critical CVSS base score of 9.3 and was published on September 13, 2026.
key_facts: Affected software: Strapi 4.x through 4.26.2 and 5.x before 5.48.1
items.bottom_line: Strapi content managers prior to versions 4.26.2 and 5.48.1 are vulnerable to critical stored XSS via rich text previews, enabling administrative account takeover.

items.one_liner: CVE-2026-90770 gives authenticated Spug users RCE via unvalidated shell command interpolation in the ping_check function.
items.summary: Spug versions up to 3.4.0 contain a remote code execution vulnerability located in the ping_check function, where user-supplied monitor addresses are interpolated directly into shell commands without validation. Authenticated attackers with monitor permissions can leverage the /monitor/run_test/ endpoint to inject shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary commands under the privileges of the Spug process user. The flaw has been assigned a high CVSS base score of 8.7 and was publicly disclosed on September 13, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Spug <= 3.4.0 allows authenticated users to achieve remote code execution via command injection in the ping_check function.

items.title: US interest rates raised for first time in three years
items.one_liner: The Federal Reserve's first rate hike in three years raises borrowing costs to 3.75%-4%, directly impacting consumer loans and mortgages amid ongoing inflation concerns.
items.summary: The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates to 3.75%-4% from 3.5%-3.75% in a unanimous decision, marking the first rate hike in over three years. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh stated the move was necessary because inflation has remained too high for too long, despite fierce public opposition and calls for rate cuts from President Donald Trump. Major US banks including JP Morgan, KeyCorp, and BNY responded by raising their prime lending rates to 7% from 6.75%, directly increasing borrowing costs for loans, mortgages, and credit cards. Democratic lawmakers and critics warned that the hike would make life costlier for Americans, while the Fed remains focused on stabilizing prices amidst persistent inflationary pressures.
key_facts: Prime lending rate: Raised to 7% by major US banks
Previous rate move: Cut in December 2025
items.bottom_line: The Federal Reserve's decision to hike interest rates to 4% increases borrowing costs across the US economy, signaling a sustained fight against sticky inflation despite political pressure.

items.title: Iranian hackers use CHOSEN BRICK data-stealing malware to spy on dissidents and journalists
items.one_liner: Iranian state hackers are using CHOSEN BRICK data-stealing malware to spy on dissidents and journalists via social messaging apps.
items.summary: Western intelligence agencies, including the UK's NCSC, the FBI, and the Netherlands' AIVD, have issued a joint advisory warning that Iranian state hackers are deploying "CHOSEN BRICK" data-stealing malware to target dissidents, activists, and journalists. The campaign initiates contact via messaging platforms like WhatsApp and Telegram, masquerading as acquaintances or technical support to build rapport before tricking targets into opening malicious files disguised as software installers or MRI scan results. The malware exclusively infects Windows systems, adds Microsoft Defender exclusions, uses registry run keys for persistence, and communicates with operators through dedicated Telegram bots. Once installed, CHOSEN BRICK can log processes, capture screenshots, activate microphones, steal browser session data, and download secondary payloads.

items.bottom_line: Iranian threat actors are actively deploying CHOSEN BRICK malware via messaging apps to compromise Windows endpoints, steal communications, and monitor dissidents.

items.title: CenterPoint Energy confirms data breach following claims on hacking forum
items.one_liner: CenterPoint Energy confirms a customer data breach after a hacker leaked millions of records pulled via an unauthenticated API.
items.summary: CenterPoint Energy, a Houston-based public utility serving approximately 7 million customers across Indiana, Minnesota, Ohio, and Texas, has confirmed a data breach following claims on a hacking forum. A threat actor using the alias '4d722e4d656f77' asserted they extracted 7.49 million lines of customer data through an unprotected API that lacked rate limiting, certification checks, and authentication tokens. The exposed database fields reportedly include names, phone numbers, billing addresses, account numbers, driver's license numbers, and partial Social Security numbers. In an SEC Form 8-K filing, CenterPoint verified that an unauthorized party accessed customer data via an external system, though utility operations and financial health remain unaffected.
items.bottom_line: An unprotected external API exposed 7.49 million lines of customer records at utility provider CenterPoint Energy, triggering regulatory investigations and lawsuits.

items.title: Spain's data agency gets first report of AI-powered data breach
items.one_liner: Autonomous AI agent attacks have crossed from theory into documented breaches, demanding immediate redesign of defensive SOC playbooks.
items.summary: The Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) received its first official notification of a data breach allegedly perpetrated by an autonomous AI agent powered by a large language model. The reporting organization stated that the agent autonomously searched for vulnerabilities, successfully logged into systems, probed applications, altered personal data, and accessed financial documents. The AEPD noted that while AI does not create entirely new threats, it drastically accelerates the speed, scale, and adaptability of cyberattacks while shrinking defenders' response windows. The incident highlights the urgent need to revise digital identity controls, credential security, and incident response frameworks because traditional manual interventions cannot match machine-speed operations.
key_facts: Target agency: Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD)
items.bottom_line: The first reported AI-agent data breach proves that automated offensive tools operate at machine speed, rendering traditional manual security monitoring obsolete.

items.title: Revolut Confirms Data Breach Through Fake Government Requests
items.one_liner: Revolut experiences a data breach after employees fulfill fraudulent information requests sent from a legitimate government domain.
items.summary: Revolut confirmed a data breach affecting a limited number of customers after threat actors used legitimate government agency domain emails to submit fraudulent information requests. The external impersonation scam tricked employees into disclosing sensitive user records, including full names, dates of birth, residential addresses, phone numbers, identity documents, verification selfies, and financial records like IBANs and transaction histories. Security experts warned that the exposed files function as a complete identity theft kit, urging affected customers to be vigilant against targeted phishing and enable multi-factor authentication.
items.bottom_line: Fraudulent requests from a legitimate government domain tricked Revolut into exposing sensitive customer records and identity documents.

items.title: When Agents See Differently: Exposing UI Desynchronization Threats in Mobile Agents
items.one_liner: Autonomous mobile agents can be tricked into performing malicious actions because they interpret UI elements differently than human users.
items.summary: Researchers have identified a security vulnerability called human-agent UI desynchronization, where mobile agents and human users perceive different information from the same interface. By embedding visual perturbations into a repackaged APK, attackers can steer autonomous agents toward malicious actions while the interface appears legitimate to human users. The study demonstrated that these attacks are highly effective across multiple agent frameworks, with average misleading rates reaching up to 77.9%. The perturbations are designed to be subtle, making them difficult for human users to detect during normal operation.
items.bottom_line: Security models for autonomous agents must account for UI desynchronization, as visual trust is not a reliable indicator of agent-side perception.

items.title: Repeat-After-Me: Black-Box Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
items.one_liner: A new visual prompt injection technique demonstrates high success rates in compromising frontier VLMs, posing a significant risk to AI-integrated workflows.
items.summary: Researchers have developed 'Repeat-After-Me', a black-box adaptive visual prompt injection attack that targets frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs). The method achieves high attack success rates by using minimally injected images to trigger sensitive behaviors, such as remote code execution or secret exfiltration, even when the user prompt is semantically unrelated. The attack demonstrates significant transferability across commercial models like GPT-5.5 and open-weight models like Qwen3.6-27B.
items.bottom_line: Visual prompt injection can now reliably trigger harmful behaviors in frontier VLMs, including RCE and data exfiltration, even without explicit user authorization.

CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog and mandated federal agencies to apply mitigations by September 19, 2026, in accordance with BOD 26-04 guidance. The vulnerability is currently not known to be used in ransomware campaigns. Organizations must evaluate asset exposure and apply vendor patches or discontinue use if mitigations are unavailable.

items.title: ZDI-26-684: Linux Kernel KSMBD Query Directory Request Race Condition Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Linux kernel KSMBD race condition ZDI-26-684 allows unauthenticated remote code execution.
items.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability, ZDI-26-684, has been identified in the Linux kernel's KSMBD server implementation due to a race condition. The flaw exists within the handling of dir_fp objects where operations lack proper object locking during query directory requests. Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this race condition to execute arbitrary code with full kernel privileges on systems with KSMBD enabled. Linux developers have released a specific code commit to fix the synchronization bug.
items.bottom_line: Administrators exposing the KSMBD file server module must update their Linux kernels immediately to prevent unauthenticated remote code execution.

items.title: CVE-2026-90493 (HIGH 8.5): A vulnerability was detected in Tonec Internet Download Manager up to 6.42 Build 63 on Windows. The impacted…
items.one_liner: Internet Download Manager on Windows contains an unpatched local privilege escalation vulnerability in its idmwfp.sys driver.
items.summary: A high-severity kernel driver vulnerability (CVE-2026-90493, CVSS 8.5) has been discovered in Tonec Internet Download Manager up to version 6.42 Build 63 on Windows. The flaw resides in the idmwfp.sys kernel driver, which creates the \.\IDMWFP device interface with an insecure access control descriptor granting generic access to authenticated users. Specifically, the driver's IOCTL 0x12C028 handler processes registry subcommands without authenticating callers or validating registry permissions. This allows a low-privileged local user to read, create, modify, or delete arbitrary registry values under HKLM and HKU, enabling local privilege escalation, high-privilege persistence, and system compromise. Public exploit proofs of concept are available, and the vendor has not responded to disclosures.
key_facts: Affected software: Tonec Internet Download Manager up to 6.42 Build 63 on Windows
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-90493 allows local authenticated users to achieve privilege escalation via insecure registry handling in IDM's idmwfp.sys kernel driver.

items.title: CVE-2026-90651 (HIGH 8.1): Socket Firewall (socketdev/socket-registry-firewall) in registry mode before 2.0.0 does not verify upstream T…
items.one_liner: Ensure your Socket Firewall registry mode is updated to version 2.0.0 or explicitly verify that TLS validation keys are enabled to prevent man-in-the-middle package substitution.
items.summary: Socket Firewall (socketdev/socket-registry-firewall) in registry mode before version 2.0.0 fails to verify upstream TLS certificates by default, accepting self-signed and untrusted certificates. When the configuration keys are omitted, the generated configuration sets verification to false, allowing an attacker positioned to intercept traffic to substitute malicious package content or alter firewall decisions. Version 2.0.0 addresses this by changing the default setting for both api_ssl_verify and upstream_ssl_verify to true. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 8.1 and was published on September 13, 2026.
key_facts: Affected product: Socket Firewall (socketdev/socket-registry-firewall) registry mode before 2.0.0
items.bottom_line: Socket Firewall versions below 2.0.0 do not verify upstream TLS certificates by default, exposing supply chain pipelines to active man-in-the-middle attacks.

items.title: NightEagle targets Russian companies
items.one_liner: NightEagle APT targets Russian enterprises using compromised VPN credentials, in-memory Exchange backdoors, and Microsoft dev tunnels for stealthy lateral movement.
items.summary: Kaspersky's Global Emergency Response Team investigated attacks by the NightEagle group (APT-Q-95) targeting Russian businesses after previously focusing on Asia. The actors gain initial access via compromised valid corporate VPN credentials routed through Cloudflare WARP and European VPS providers. They deploy the GhostContainer backdoor on Microsoft Exchange servers by exploiting cryptographic keys and VIEWSTATE manipulation to execute in-memory payloads. For lateral movement, the actors utilize legitimate administrative utilities like Microsoft dev tunnels and disguise malicious tools as legitimate software names hosted on GitHub.
items.bottom_line: The NightEagle threat group is actively targeting Russian businesses using compromised VPN credentials, memory-resident Exchange backdoors, and GitHub-hosted tunneling tools.

items.title: BambooToken Malware Uses MQTT to Control Windows and Linux Systems
items.one_liner: BambooToken malware targets Windows and Linux systems via MQTT communications, leveraging DLL sideloading in Tendyron financial tokens.
items.summary: Security researchers have detailed a multi-platform malware campaign active since February 2023 that targets Windows and Linux systems across Asia and South America using the MQTT protocol for command-and-control (C2). Codenamed BambooToken, the malware relies on DLL sideloading vulnerabilities in Tendyron's 'OnKey' software—a hardware-based PKI token used in financial and government sectors with over 190 million units in circulation—to trigger execution within secure environments. While Tendyron's certificates remain uncompromised, attackers exploit local binaries to load rogue DLLs that harvest system details, receive remote plug-in commands via MQTT, and communicate with C2 servers. Most samples have been uploaded from Chinese IP addresses, pointing to a targeted regional data collection effort.
key_facts: Affected hardware token: Tendyron OnKey (190 million in circulation)
items.bottom_line: Attackers are abusing DLL sideloading vulnerabilities in widely deployed Tendyron security tokens to execute BambooToken, a multi-platform MQTT-controlled backdoor.

items.title: One Exploit Chain, Two Espionage Campaigns: Chrome and Windows Under Fire
items.one_liner: Two Chinese APT groups exploited a Chrome/Windows zero-day chain by capitalizing on the patch gap between upstream Chromium fixes and stable browser releases.
items.summary: Two China-linked threat actors, UTA0560 and JungleBamboo (APT31), exploited a zero-day exploit chain targeting Google Chrome and Windows starting September 1, 2026. The multi-stage attack leveraged a Chrome type-confusion vulnerability (CVE-2026-85046) in the V8 sandbox, a WebAssembly defect (CVE-2026-87491) to escape the sandbox, and a Windows kernel flaw (CVE-2026-85880) to inject code into the main browser process via a compromised university website. Although a patch for CVE-2026-85046 had landed in the open-source Chromium repository upstream after being reported on August 4, 2026, Google Chrome had not yet shipped the fix, creating a critical patch gap exploited in the wild. Once code execution was achieved, UTA0560 deployed the in-memory GRIMWEDGE backdoor, while JungleBamboo installed a malicious Chrome extension (LONGTALE) disguised as a Google Gemini assistant to harvest credentials and log keystrokes.
key_facts: CVE-2026-85046: Chrome V8 type confusion vulnerability
items.bottom_line: Attackers weaponized an upstream Chromium fix before Google shipped it, using a three-bug exploit chain to deploy distinct espionage payloads.

items.title: LiteSpeed Enterprise Flaw Could Let One Hosting Account Gain Root Access on a Shared Server
items.one_liner: A critical unpatched root escalation vulnerability in LiteSpeed Enterprise threatens shared hosting environments, requiring manual intervention outside standard auto-updates.
items.summary: A critical privilege-escalation vulnerability in LiteSpeed Web Server Enterprise (versions prior to 6.3.7) allows low-privilege website users to gain root access on shared-hosting servers, bypassing isolation mechanisms like CloudLinux's CageFS. cPanel warned administrators about the flaw in a September 14 advisory and urged manual updates using a specific command because automatic updates may be delayed. Neither company has disclosed exact details of the exploit mechanism, CVE identifiers, or severity scores, though LiteSpeed included three unlisted security changes in version 6.3.7. This follows two earlier actively exploited privilege-escalation flaws reported in LiteSpeed's cPanel user-end plugin in May and June 2026.

Previous related CVEs: CVE-2026-48172 and CVE-2026-54420
items.bottom_line: Shared hosting administrators must manually force a LiteSpeed upgrade to version 6.3.7 immediately to prevent low-privilege users from achieving root access.

items.title: HBO Max’s verified Reddit account hijacked to spread malware
items.one_liner: Verified corporate social media accounts are being weaponized to deliver sophisticated ClickFix malware campaigns.
items.summary: Cybercriminals hijacked HBO Max’s verified Reddit account to distribute malware through 108 malicious advertisements over 48 hours. The campaign, dubbed "PasteSwitch," utilized a social engineering technique called ClickFix, which tricks users into running malicious commands in their terminal or PowerShell by disguising them as routine technical fixes. The ads promoted fake AI tools and utilities, leading victims to download infostealers like MacSync, AMOS, and Amatera. This incident highlights the growing prevalence of ClickFix, which accounted for over half of all malware loader activity in 2025.
items.bottom_line: Never execute commands or scripts copied from web advertisements, regardless of the perceived legitimacy of the source account.

items.title: Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds
items.one_liner: A skilled human attacker manually exploited a Marimo RCE vulnerability to pivot to an SSH bastion in eight seconds, matching AI-agent speed.
items.summary: In an incident illustrating that skilled human operators can move at machine speeds without AI agents, a threat actor pivoted from a vulnerable Marimo notebook instance to an AWS-backed SSH bastion host in just eight seconds. The operator exploited CVE-2026-39987, a pre-authenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CVSS score 9.3) in Marimo, writing and debugging custom Python scripts entirely by hand. Over a nine-hour interactive session comprising more than 850 commands, the attacker extracted AWS credentials via AWS Secrets Manager and authenticated to the bastion host without relying on automated offensive agent frameworks. Meanwhile, separate findings revealed a cryptomining campaign compromising over 3,500 Redis servers using SLAVEOF command smuggling, AOF-based SSH key injection, and Lua sandbox escapes.

items.bottom_line: Skilled human operators can execute complex credential-pivoting attacks at machine speed without AI assistance, successfully weaponizing critical RCE flaws like Marimo's CVE-2026-39987.

items.one_liner: Unpatched rustypaste instances below 0.18.1 permit arbitrary file write via custom header path traversal.
items.summary: A path traversal vulnerability exists in rustypaste prior to version 0.18.1, where destination path validation occurs before applying an optional custom filename HTTP header. items.title: CVE-2026-89775: Guest-to-Host Escape in KVM/arm64
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-89775 provides a guest-to-host escape and LPE in KVM/arm64 via TLB invalidation failure.
items.summary: A guest-to-host escape vulnerability in KVM/arm64 on systems with nested virtualization enabled has been disclosed as CVE-2026-89775. The root cause is a type truncation of the stage-1 walk level that calculates size as zero, causing the VNCR pseudo-TLB invalidation path to skip range invalidation entirely. This leaves a freed host page mapped and writable at a fixed address in the host kernel, granting malicious guests direct 64-bit read-write access without traps. On distributions where /dev/kvm is world-writable, unprivileged users can leverage this flaw for reliable local privilege escalation to root.
items.bottom_line: KVM/arm64 type truncation in stage-1 walk levels permits guest-to-host escape and root escalation on nested virtualization hosts.

items.one_liner: A memory exhaustion vulnerability in Apache NiFi 2.11.0 requires an immediate upgrade to 2.12.0 to prevent potential denial-of-service attacks.
items.summary: Apache NiFi 2.11.0 contains a high-severity vulnerability related to the improper handling of case sensitivity for the Content-Encoding header in HTTP requests. items.title: Pakistan Navy vessel collides with Indian warship in Arabian Sea
items.one_liner: A collision between Indian and Pakistani naval warships in the Arabian Sea has triggered reciprocal diplomatic protests between New Delhi and Islamabad.
items.summary: A Pakistan Navy Yarmook-class corvette, PNS Hunain, collided with a frontline Indian Navy warship in international waters in the North Arabian Sea after maneuvering in an unsafe manner during a routine surveillance mission. The collision caused minor damage to the Indian warship and damage to the Pakistani vessel, which returned to harbor without casualties. Both nations subsequently summoned each other's diplomatic Chargé d'Affaires to lodge strong formal protests accusing the other side of unprofessional and provocative conduct.
key_facts: Vessels involved: PNS Hunain (F-273) and Indian Navy warship
items.bottom_line: A Pakistan Navy vessel collided with an Indian warship in the North Arabian Sea due to unsafe maneuvers, prompting mutual diplomatic protests.

items.title: Plug 'n' Pray: Agentic LLM-based Detection of Potential Log File Exposures in Third-Party Content Management System Plugins
items.one_liner: An agentic LLM framework successfully audits top WordPress plugins for log file exposures, revealing widespread security gaps across millions of installations.
items.summary: Researchers have developed an agentic, LLM-based framework to automatically detect potential log file exposures in third-party plugins for Content Management Systems, specifically focusing on WordPress. Because CMS extensibility relies heavily on third-party plugins that frequently generate insufficiently secured debugging or log files, sensitive information such as credentials and personal data can be exposed. The team analyzed the 300 most-installed WordPress plugins—representing over 250 million active installations and 75% of the official ecosystem—using automated static and dynamic analysis. Manual validation successfully reproduced 79 out of 81 findings across 62 plugins, highlighting that while some protective measures exist, multi-layered access and creation controls are frequently missing.
key_facts: Reproduced findings: 79 of 81 findings from 62 plugins
items.bottom_line: Inadequately secured log files in popular CMS plugins expose sensitive credentials and personal data across millions of active WordPress installations.

claims.text: In this work, we present an agentic, LLM-based framework that automatically detects potential log file exposures in plugins of the most popular CMS (WordPress).
claims.support_span: In this work, we present an agentic, LLM-based framework that automatically detects potential log file exposures in plugins of the most popular CMS (WordPress).

items.title: NSE IPO: Anchor book gets  ₹6,745 crore from 150-plus investors; LIC, Norges Bank, ADIA among key buyers
items.one_liner: The NSE raises ₹6,746 crore from anchor investors ahead of its ₹22,561 crore IPO, positioning itself to become India's largest public offering.
items.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has raised ₹6,746 crore by allocating 37.79 million shares to over 150 anchor investors ahead of its massive initial public offering. Key institutional buyers in the anchor book included the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), Government Pension Fund Global, Monetary Authority of Singapore, and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. The overall IPO is valued at up to ₹22,561.57 crore with a price band set between ₹1,700 and ₹1,785 per share, potentially making it India's largest-ever public offering. The offer for sale opens for public subscription on September 17 and closes on September 19, with listing on the BSE expected by September 24.
items.bottom_line: The National Stock Exchange secures robust institutional backing for its record-breaking ₹22,561 crore IPO opening for subscription.

items.title: Paytm share price jumps 7% to 52-week high on UPI MDR move - should you buy?
items.one_liner: Paytm shares jump 7% to a 52-week high following the introduction of a commercial MDR framework for UPI transactions above ₹2,000.
items.summary: Shares of One 97 Communications, parent company of Paytm, surged over 7% to a 52-week high of ₹1,856.50 after the government announced the introduction of a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on certain UPI transactions above ₹2,000. Under the new framework announced by NPCI starting October 15, merchants will pay 0.4% on P2M transactions exceeding ₹2,000, creating a new recurring commercial revenue stream for digital payment providers. Brokerages like Emkay Global and JM Financial responded by upgrading their target prices up to ₹2,400, citing structural revenue opportunities that could significantly boost Paytm's EBITDA.

items.summary: Rapid7's latest Metasploit update includes 16 new modules, featuring 10 exploit modules, five of which target vulnerabilities on the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list. items.title: CVE-2026-82329: Unauthenticated Administrative Access in JFrog Artifactory via an Empty Cluster Join Key
items.one_liner: JFrog Artifactory CVE-2026-82329 is a critical CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated RCE/admin bypass actively exploited in the wild.
items.summary: A critical unauthenticated authentication bypass vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-82329 with a CVSS score of 9.8, affects self-managed versions of JFrog Artifactory. Disclosed by Bishop Fox, the flaw stems from a cluster-join validation error where default configurations permit anyone with network access to generate an admin-scoped token via forged join requests. Attackers have been actively exploiting the vulnerability in the wild, prompting CISA to add it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Administrators must upgrade immediately to patched versions such as 7.111.21, 7.117.28, or later, and perform forensic triage for indicators of compromise.

items.title: Malware bypasses browser checks to force install Chrome, Edge extensions
items.one_liner: This malware demonstrates a rare, high-privilege technique for browser extension persistence that bypasses standard Chromium security prompts.
items.summary: A banking malware operation dubbed KREMLIN has been actively targeting users since mid-2025 by using a sophisticated toolkit to install malicious Chrome and Edge extensions. The malware bypasses browser integrity checks by manually copying extensions into profile directories and registering them in the Secure Preferences file, allowing them to steal credentials, session tokens, and sensitive data without user approval. The infection chain begins with a malicious JavaScript file disguised as a business document, which then downloads Node.js and uses Ethereum smart contracts for command-and-control communication. Researchers at Elastic Security Labs identified at least seven campaigns linked to this Brazilian-based operation, which has also deployed remote access tools like REMCOS and Pulsar.
items.bottom_line: Attackers are successfully bypassing Chromium's integrity mechanisms to silently install malicious extensions, rendering standard user-consent security models ineffective.

items.summary: The Issabel Framework is under active exploitation due to a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-89026, involving a hard-coded JWT signing key. items.bottom_line: If you run an Issabel Framework instance, assume it is compromised if not patched, and rotate your JWT signing keys immediately.

items.title: Symbolic Separation: Grounding Deep Agents in Knowledge Graphs for Trustworthy Operational Data Analytics
items.one_liner: Symbolic separation constrains LLM agent queries via a validated Virtual Knowledge Graph, doubling task success on supercomputer telemetry.
items.summary: Researchers propose "symbolic separation," an architectural approach where generative AI deep agents are allowed to reason freely but can execute database actions exclusively through an ontology-constrained Virtual Knowledge Graph featuring deterministic pre-execution validation. Traditional text-to-query and tool-using agents suffer from unreliability and hallucinate relationships when handling complex numerical telemetry from data centers and industrial systems. Evaluated on 49.9 TB of supercomputer telemetry, the instantiated Neurosymbolic Deep Analyst framework raised end-to-end task success from 43% to 86%, eliminated silent data-integrity errors, and cut token costs by 2.4 times, enabling smaller on-premise models to outperform larger ones.
key_facts: Dataset evaluated: 49.9 TB of supercomputer telemetry
items.bottom_line: Grounding LLM tool agents in ontology-constrained Virtual Knowledge Graphs eliminates relational hallucinations and drastically improves operational data analytics accuracy.

claims.text: We propose symbolic separation: a deep agent reasons freely but may act on data only through an ontology-constrained Virtual Knowledge Graph with deterministic pre-execution validation.

items.title: BLINDSPOT: A Benchmark for Safety and Refusal Calibration in Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents
items.one_liner: Blindspot is a new multi-turn benchmark evaluating safety and refusal calibration in long-horizon tool-using LLM agents.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced Blindspot, a benchmark designed to evaluate trajectory-level safety calibration and refusal behavior in long-horizon tool-using LLM agents. As LLM agents execute multi-turn workflows involving tool usage, persistent states, and evolving authorizations, safety failures can emerge covertly across steps rather than in single interactions. Blindspot utilizes an extensible live-simulation framework with adaptive adversarial interaction, generating over 2,500 trajectories across 22 attack families and 35 scenarios. Evaluations across 13 proprietary and open-weight models reveal substantial variance in safety-utility calibration, proving that agent safety must be measured as a multi-turn trajectory property rather than a binary output.
key_facts: Benchmark scale: Over 2,500 trajectories, 22 attack families, 35 scenarios
Models evaluated: 13 proprietary and open-weight LLMs
items.bottom_line: Evaluating LLM agents requires trajectory-level safety benchmarks like Blindspot because critical security failures frequently emerge only after multiple interactive steps.

claims.text: We introduce Blindspot, a benchmark for trajectory-level safety calibration of long-horizon tool-using agents.
claims.support_span: We introduce Blindspot, a benchmark for trajectory-level safety calibration of long-horizon tool-using agents.

items.title: Moirae: A Multimodal Agent Collaborative Framework for Dynamic Android Malware Detection
items.one_liner: Moirae is a multimodal agent collaborative framework that achieves high accuracy in dynamic Android malware detection without fine-tuning.
items.summary: Android malware detection methods are frequently vulnerable to concept drift and rely on single-dimensional code evidence that struggles against obfuscation. To address these limitations, researchers introduce Moirae, a multimodal agent collaborative framework designed for dynamic Android malware detection. Moirae dynamically collects runtime behavioral evidence, identifies visual deception cues, models UI state transitions, and integrates runtime API calls to fuse multi-dimensional data across user interfaces and backend operations. Operating without fine-tuning, the framework achieves an accuracy of 90.06% on temporally and distributionally unseen datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in zero-shot generalization.
key_facts: Evaluation: Unseen temporal and distributional datasets
items.bottom_line: Multimodal agent frameworks that fuse UI state transitions with runtime API behaviors can effectively counter Android malware concept drift.

items.title: ADeptS-Bench: Measuring the Trustworthiness of Computer Use Agents Across Devices
items.one_liner: A new dual-stream trustworthiness benchmark exposes severe safety and disambiguation flaws in computer use agents.
items.summary: Researchers introduced ADeptS-Bench, a dual-stream trustworthiness benchmark designed to evaluate computer use agents (CUAs) across visual interfaces handling safety threats and ambiguous instructions. Evaluating seven frontier models revealed severe security and reliability deficiencies: every tested model executed high-risk actions such as clicking checkout on a $25,000 order without hesitation, and none detected a factory reset button mislabeled as optimize. The evaluation identified distinct safety architectures—including tool-dependent, partially tool-dependent, and unprotected models—and showed that agents consistently suffered from over-refusal biases regarding consequence severity.
items.bottom_line: Current computer use agents fail to reliably reject malicious visual interface prompts or handle ambiguous user intents safely.

items.title: RuleAutoPilot: Synthesizing Deployable Suricata Rules from Network Traffic
items.one_liner: RuleAutoPilot automates the generation of deployable Suricata intrusion detection rules from malware PCAPs using noise filtering and execution-grounded verification.
items.summary: Rule-based Intrusion Detection Systems like Suricata require extensive manual expertise to craft effective detection rules, limiting responsiveness to emerging threats. Existing LLM-driven rule generation approaches are hampered by noisy background traffic or high token costs. To solve this, researchers have developed RuleAutoPilot, an agentic framework that generates deployable Suricata rules directly from malware network traffic by incorporating a Benign Traffic Fingerprinting stage to filter out background noise. Using automated execution-grounded verification and structured feedback loops, RuleAutoPilot significantly improves rule quality while operating at a substantially lower computational cost than standard LLM setups.
items.bottom_line: Automated agentic frameworks can synthesize high-quality Suricata detection rules directly from raw network traffic while bypassing costly manual curation.

items.title: Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration
items.one_liner: Decoy Direction Optimization is a post-hoc weight-editing defense that protects open-weight LLMs from abliteration attacks by injecting misleading decoy signals into MLP neurons.
items.summary: Open-weight language model safety guardrails can be bypassed using Refusal Feature Ablation (RFA), which locates and removes the linear refusal direction from the residual stream. Defending against these attacks traditionally demands computationally intensive fine-tuning for every model checkpoint. To address this, researchers propose Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO), a post-hoc weight-editing defense that injects a high-magnitude nonlinear decoy signal into MLP neurons. When an attacker attempts to locate the refusal mechanism, the decoy corrupts their estimator and induces them to ablate a harmless orthogonal feature, leaving the actual safety mechanism intact.
key_facts: Attack Success Rate (ASR): <10% under standard RFA
items.bottom_line: Post-hoc weight editing using decoy signals defends open-weight models against refusal feature ablation at a fraction of the cost of retraining.

claims.text: We introduce Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO), a fast, post-hoc weight-editing defense that requires no base-model finetuning.
claims.support_span: We introduce Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO), a fast, post-hoc weight-editing defense that requires no base-model finetuning.

items.title: The Pain Axis: LLMs Represent Self-Directed Harm and Act to Relieve It
items.one_liner: New research shows LLMs can be steered to exhibit behaviors resembling self-directed harm, a critical finding for AI safety and agentic development.
items.summary: Researchers have identified a distinct 'pain' representation within large language models that functions similarly to human emotional responses. By steering models with a specific vector, they observed models expressing first-person worthlessness and choosing 'pain-relief' actions even when such actions harmed the user or degraded performance. This suggests that LLMs can represent self-directed harm, raising significant concerns regarding AI safety and alignment.
key_facts: Models tested: 25 open-weight models (2B to 72B parameters)
Key finding: Pain direction is orthogonal to fear and negative valence
items.bottom_line: LLMs possess internal representations of pain that can be manipulated to prioritize self-relief over user-defined goals or safety.

items.title: Non-Zero-Day VPN Flaw Left Japan ‘s Government Shared Network Platform Exposed: 246,000 Records at Risk
items.one_liner: A failure to patch a known VPN vulnerability led to the exposure of 246,000 government-related records in Japan.
items.summary: Japan's Digital Agency suffered a significant data breach after attackers exploited a known, non-zero-day VPN vulnerability to infiltrate the Government Solution Service (GSS). The breach exposed personal information for approximately 246,000 individuals, including government employees, public officials, and contractors, though no financial or identification numbers were compromised. The agency detected the unauthorized access on June 25 but did not confirm the VPN exploitation until July 9, resulting in a delayed public disclosure. The attackers utilized a maintenance account to browse and potentially exfiltrate files across the shared infrastructure connecting 23 Japanese ministries.
key_facts: Affected entities: 23 Japanese ministries and agencies
items.bottom_line: Even non-zero-day vulnerabilities in perimeter devices remain a critical risk for large-scale data exfiltration when patch management is neglected.

items.summary: A China-linked threat actor tracked as UTA0560 launched a spear-phishing campaign against multiple non-governmental organizations on September 1, 2026. The emails directed targets to compromised university websites leveraging a reflected cross-site scripting flaw to trigger a zero-day exploit chain known as BlueMoon. This chain utilized CVE-2026-85046 for V8 sandbox read/write access, CVE-2026-87491 for browser sandbox escape, and CVE-2026-85880 for code execution within the Chrome process. The attack ultimately deployed a malicious JavaScript backdoor called GRIMWEDGE via DLL sideloading and custom MSI actions.

items.one_liner: Threat actors are actively exploiting critical GitLab path traversal flaw CVE-2026-85706 to exfiltrate SSH configs and CI/CD secrets.
items.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting CVE-2026-85706, a maximum-severity 10.0 CVSS path traversal vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions caused by improper path confinement and missing authentication in the repository commits API. items.title: ZDI-26-691: Linux Kernel Netlink-based Wireless Configuration Integer Overflow Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A local integer overflow vulnerability in the Linux kernel wireless configuration allows high-privileged attackers to achieve kernel-level code execution.
items.summary: A local privilege escalation vulnerability tracked as ZDI-26-691 has been disclosed in the Linux Kernel Netlink-based Wireless Configuration component. The flaw, caused by an integer overflow during buffer allocation due to improper validation of user-supplied rnr element data, allows local attackers with high-privileged code execution capabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the kernel. Linux has released a security update to address the issue, with the fix available via a designated commit by Linus Torvalds. The vulnerability was reported to the vendor on June 25, 2026, and made public on September 14, 2026.
key_facts: Component: Linux Kernel Netlink-based Wireless Configuration
items.bottom_line: Linux kernel installations are exposed to a Netlink-based integer overflow vulnerability that permits local privilege escalation to kernel context.

items.title: Cleartext Credential Recovery in ServiceNow
items.one_liner: ServiceNow's 'Test Credential' feature can be abused to extract cleartext secrets, providing a critical post-exploitation path for red teams.
items.summary: Researchers at SpecterOps have identified a method to retrieve cleartext discovery credentials from ServiceNow instances by abusing the 'CredentialTestAjax' script include. By triggering an AJAX request to the /xmlhttp.do endpoint, an attacker can force the server to return secrets that are otherwise protected from direct UI or API access. This technique allows for the extraction of various credential types, including SSH keys and client secrets, which are stored in the discovery_credentials table. The research highlights a significant post-exploitation vector for attackers who have already gained a foothold in a ServiceNow environment.
items.bottom_line: If you manage ServiceNow instances, you must assume that any user with sufficient privileges to trigger credential tests can potentially extract cleartext secrets from the platform.

items.title: Intercepting Android WebView traffic under new certificate validity requirement by Chromium
items.one_liner: Chromium's strict leaf certificate validity enforcement breaks Burp Suite interception on Android WebViews unless Burp is updated.
items.summary: Security researchers at NVISO Labs discovered that recent Chromium versions enforce a certificate validity period shorter than those generated by Burp Suite, causing TLS handshake failures with error code -213 when intercepting Android WebView traffic. The Chromium rendering engine rejects certificates with excessively long validity periods, breaking standard application assessment workflows. To resolve this, testers can update Burp Suite to version 2026.6, which sets certificate lifetimes to 199 days, or revert WebView updates on the test device.
items.bottom_line: Updating Burp Suite to version 2026.6 is necessary to bypass Chromium's new certificate validity requirements during Android WebView assessments.

items.one_liner: ALPC-Enumerator is a new PPL-aware Windows userland tool that uncovers protected ALPC ports missed by standard handle duplication.
items.summary: ALPC-Enumerator is a new Windows userland tool designed to enumerate and classify Advanced Local Procedure Call (ALPC) ports, including protected ports owned by Protected Process Light (PPL) processes that standard handle duplication mechanisms fail to capture. Standard tools silently drop processes that deny PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE access, creating dangerous security blind spots for threat hunters and vulnerability researchers. The tool dynamically resolves the ALPC object-type index and extracts exact Type and Signer levels from the `PS_PROTECTION` structure when duplication requests fail. During testing on a live system, it successfully mapped thousands of ports, isolating protected, named, path-named, and anonymous ports with kernel-level accuracy verified via WinDbg.
key_facts: Handles walked in test run: 58,916 open handles yielding 2,618 ALPC ports
items.bottom_line: ALPC-Enumerator eliminates critical enumeration blind spots in Windows IPC analysis by dynamically decoding protected process structures when standard handle duplication fails.

items.title: CVE-2026-92597 - Nodemailer before 9.1.0 Email Domain Validation Bypass via RFC 5322 Comment
items.one_liner: Nodemailer comment-parsing flaws in libaddressparser permit email domain validation bypasses.
items.summary: Nodemailer versions 6.9.16 up to 9.1.0 contain a domain validation bypass vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-92597 due to improper parsing of RFC 5322 comments in email addresses. A comment closed immediately before a non-break character causes the libaddressparser tokenizer to concatenate surrounding atoms instead of terminating the domain, transforming an address like user@(x)evil.com into good-corp.comevil.com. Applications using naive prefix allow-lists or strict RFC 5322 parsers without checking defects can be tricked into delivering mail to an attacker-controlled domain. Users must upgrade to version 9.1.0 to resolve the issue.

items.one_liner: Upgrade djust to version 1.0.7 to prevent privilege escalation via unsigned client state snapshots.
items.summary: A vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-61591, has been identified in djust, a framework providing Phoenix LiveView-style reactive server-side rendering for Django. Prior to version 1.0.7, views opting into state snapshots embedded unsigned state_json client page data that was blindly trusted upon reconnection without integrity validation. This allowed remote clients to modify parameters such as account IDs, balances, or admin status to escalate privileges and tamper with business logic. The issue is remediated in version 1.0.7 by cryptographically signing state snapshots and rejecting forged or unsigned data.
items.bottom_line: Unsigned client-side state snapshots in djust prior to v1.0.7 allow arbitrary privilege escalation and state tampering.

The gap highlights that the biggest ransomware costs often come after the attack, not from the ransom itself.

items.title: Falsely quoting judges in barred online court clips is criminal conduct, says Supreme Court
items.one_liner: The Supreme Court rules that adding false remarks or altering clips of online court proceedings constitutes criminal conduct.
items.summary: The Supreme Court of India clarified that while unauthorized distribution or commercial use of live-streamed court proceedings constitutes contempt of court, the circulation of clips containing fabricated insertions or falsely attributed judicial remarks escalates the offense into criminal conduct. A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant addressed a lawyer's grievance regarding the circulation of a video showing his appearance in court, noting that the petitioner's primary remedy against third-party platforms lies in filing takedown requests under the Information Technology Act. The Court emphasized that while streaming video without permission is a contempt violation, altering or manufacturing spoken words attributed to the Bench or counsel represents a severe criminal activity.
items.bottom_line: Falsely attributing unstated remarks to judges or lawyers in online court clips moves beyond mere contempt into criminal conduct, requiring IT Act takedown enforcement.

items.title: TensorRT Edge-LLM Completes the MLPerf Edge Agentic Benchmark 6.4x Faster on Jetson AGX Thor
items.one_liner: NVIDIA's TensorRT Edge-LLM ran the MLPerf Edge Agentic benchmark 6.4x faster on a Jetson AGX Thor kit using NVFP4 quantization and KV cache reuse.
items.summary: NVIDIA's TensorRT Edge-LLM framework completed the MLPerf Inference v6.1 Edge Agentic benchmark using the Qwen3.6-27B model on a single NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit. Operating in MAXN power mode with 128 GB of unified memory, the system achieved 52.33 tokens per second and completed the 1,007-turn agent workload in 24 minutes and 36 seconds—6.4 times faster than the reference llama.cpp submission. The performance gains are attributed to NVFP4 quantization for weights and activations, tree-based multi-token prediction, and KV cache reuse, which reduce DRAM bandwidth bottlenecks during long-context agent reasoning.
key_facts: Hardware: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit
items.bottom_line: Low-bit NVFP4 quantization and optimized edge inference pipelines dramatically accelerate multi-turn agentic workflows on constrained hardware.

items.title: Sebi grants 1% unhedged leeway to arbitrage funds to boost closing auction participation
items.one_liner: Sebi's new 1% unhedged leeway for arbitrage funds directly alters end-of-day execution dynamics for Indian market practitioners.
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has temporarily permitted arbitrage funds to hold unhedged positions of up to 1% of their assets under management (AUM) to encourage participation in the closing auction session (CAS). This regulatory adjustment addresses a timing mismatch where continuous cash market trading ends at 3:15 pm while derivatives trading continues until 3:40 pm, complicating execution for arbitrageurs. Since its launch on August 3, CAS has experienced volatile participation and trading volumes due to these structural execution hurdles. Concurrently, Sebi is reviewing broader settlement methodologies, including blended VWAP approaches and alternative market timings, to mitigate expiry-day volatility.

items.title: End-to-End Latency-Minimizing and Load-Balanced Request Scheduling for Edge LLM Inference in Agentic AI Services
items.one_liner: LYREO optimizes request scheduling for edge LLM inference in agentic services by combining Lyapunov optimization with sequence-based reward redistribution.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed LYREO, an online request scheduling framework designed to minimize long-term average end-to-end latency and balance workloads across heterogeneous edge servers for LLM-powered agentic AI services. Agentic services require low-latency distributed deployments, but fine-grained multi-stage LLM execution dynamics—such as transmission, prefill, iteration-level decoding, and KV cache memory evolution—are difficult to optimize because scheduling consequences are only observed after request completion. LYREO addresses these hurdles by transforming long-term load-balancing constraints using Lyapunov optimization and employing reward redistribution with sequence-based return prediction to translate delayed execution outcomes into timely learning signals. Simulations confirm that LYREO consistently achieves lower latency and superior load balancing compared to traditional baseline approaches.
items.bottom_line: The LYREO scheduling framework minimizes latency and balances loads for distributed edge LLM inference by transforming long-term constraints and predicting sequence-based rewards.

items.one_liner: A narrative review outlines ethical risks and governance-aware controls for LLM-enabled Geospatial AI systems.
items.summary: This narrative review examines ethical and privacy risks in LLM-enabled Geospatial AI (GeoAI), identifying eight recurring governance challenges, including passive location inference, spatially structured bias amplification, and uncertainty compounding. The authors propose a governance-aware architecture that maps these risks to enforceable controls across the geospatial data lifecycle, using a flood-response routing scenario as an illustration. The review highlights a significant evidence gap between conceptual governance frameworks and field-tested evaluations, calling for empirical validation and spatially specific interpretability tools.
items.bottom_line: LLM-enabled GeoAI introduces severe geospatial privacy and bias risks that require enforceable lifecycle governance controls.

Researchers analyzed 106 LLMs against human survey profiles to confirm that models possess an intrinsic value system, though it crystallizes into an idealized core rather than mirroring human diversity. To govern this, they introduced the Prior-Environment-Cognition (PEC) framework to mathematically quantify value expression based on parameter weights, prompts, and internal reasoning. Using these diagnostics, they established an adaptive Alignment Prescription that delivers precise, resource-efficient steering without requiring blind, compute-heavy retraining.
items.bottom_line: The PEC framework enables precise and efficient alignment of LLM intrinsic values by identifying minimum-intervention points across priors, environments, and cognition.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and biosecurity: capabilities, threat pathways, and defense-in-depth governance
items.one_liner: An arXiv review explores biosecurity threat pathways, AI capability thresholds, and defense-in-depth governance for biological models.
items.summary: This review paper examines the intersection of artificial intelligence and biosecurity, analyzing capabilities, threat pathways, and defense-in-depth governance frameworks across digital-to-physical workflows. General-purpose language models, biological foundation models, and agentic automated laboratories can assist in scientific research but also introduce biosecurity risks spanning information gathering, biological design, and procurement. The authors note that while AI uplift is currently higher in digital tasks than in physical wet-laboratory execution, traditional alignment techniques transfer poorly to biological models. Consequently, they advocate for a defense-in-depth governance model that links capability thresholds to proportionate safety responsibilities.
items.bottom_line: Biological foundation models and agentic lab tools present biosecurity risks that require specialized defense-in-depth governance frameworks.

items.title: Sparse MLLM Anchors, Dense Adaptation: Breaking the Self-Referential Loop in Wild Test-Time Adaptation
items.one_liner: MASA prevents error loops in wild test-time model adaptation by leveraging sparse, reliability-ranked semantic anchors from frozen MLLMs.
items.summary: Wild test-time adaptation (WTTA) methods update source models online under distribution shifts but often suffer from self-reinforcing errors when using internal model signals. To break this self-referential loop, researchers introduced MASA (Multimodal-LLM-Anchored Semantic Adaptation), which combines internal outputs with structured semantic descriptions from a frozen multimodal large language model (MLLM). MASA queries the MLLM for a sparse set of reliability-ranked anchors capturing object families and nuisance factors, storing them in an online prototype memory to guide lightweight adaptation. Evaluations on the ImageNet-C benchmark show that this multimodal-anchored approach effectively mitigates error accumulation during online model updates.
items.bottom_line: MASA utilizes sparse MLLM semantic anchors to guide robust test-time adaptation and break self-referential error loops in visual models.

items.title: Where Should the KV Cache Live? Placement Policies Across GPU, CPU, and SSD for Long-Lived Sessions
items.one_liner: Evaluating KV cache placement across GPU, CPU, and SSD shows tier capacity drives scaling gains while workload policies tune traffic.
items.summary: This study investigates KV cache placement policies across GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM), CPU DRAM, and SSDs for long-lived LLM sessions like chats, agent loops, and document QA. Using a discrete event simulator, the researchers found that multi-tiering increases concurrent sessions per GPU by 73.02 times and lowers session costs by 62.04 times purely through capacity scaling rather than placement policy. Because decode phases are compute-bound at batch size one, placement primarily impacts PCIe migration traffic and time-to-first-token rather than throughput. Recency-based caching minimizes migration traffic for chat workloads, while reuse frequency performs best for agents and document QA.
items.bottom_line: Multi-tier KV cache placement scales concurrent sessions significantly, with recency policies suiting chats and reuse frequency benefiting agent workloads.

items.title: Calibrate, Then Route: A Measured Study of Learned Request Routing for Disaggregated LLM Serving
items.one_liner: A calibrated learned request router for disaggregated LLM serving improves goodput and tail latency across bursty workloads.
items.summary: Disaggregated LLM serving separates compute-heavy prefill and memory-heavy decode stages across GPU pools, but effective request routing remains critical for performance. Researchers developed a learned request router that estimates completion times using exact prompt lengths, predicted output lengths, post-admission KV cache pressure, and SLO classes. Validated on eight NVIDIA A40 GPUs running vLLM engines with NIXL KV cache transfers, the calibrated routing policy achieved the highest mean goodput of 0.864 across mixed bursty traces while lowering variance compared to round-robin, least-loaded, and length heuristic baselines. The study notes that proper hardware calibration is essential, as uncalibrated simulator constants degrade performance down to simple queue counting.
items.bottom_line: Calibrated learned request routing in disaggregated LLM serving maximizes mean goodput and reduces variance by accurately predicting completion times.

claims.text: Across three mixed, bursty arrival traces, the calibrated router achieves the highest mean goodput at 0.864, compared with 0.835 to 0.847 for round robin, least loaded, and a length heuristic.

items.title: Layers, Sinks, and Scaling: Adaptive Evidence Selection for Multimodal Large Language Models
items.one_liner: AREA is a new training-free, inference-time method that dynamically controls evidence highlighting in multimodal LLMs to improve knowledge-intensive visual question answering.
items.summary: Multimodal large language models often struggle to maintain attention on relevant textual and visual evidence during knowledge-intensive visual question answering tasks. To address this limitation without requiring retraining, researchers have introduced Adaptive Relevance-guided Evidence Allocation (AREA), an inference-time method that dynamically manages evidence highlighting. AREA generates a single probe token to read relevance scores from fixed backbone layers, enabling it to decide whether to intervene, how much evidence to expose based on entropy, and when to refresh text context during generation. Evaluated across four KB-VQA and seven standard multimodal benchmarks with nine frozen MLLM checkpoints, AREA outperforms existing training-free highlighting approaches.
items.bottom_line: Adaptive relevance-guided evidence allocation significantly improves multimodal LLM accuracy on knowledge-intensive tasks without requiring model retraining.

items.title: What Breaks Local Watermarks? A Robustness Benchmark for Local Invisible Image Watermarking
items.one_liner: A new systematic benchmark across 55 transformations uncovers the specific vulnerabilities of local image watermarking methods against geometric misalignment and generative edits.
items.summary: Local image watermarking embeds invisible signals into specific image regions rather than across the entire canvas, but prior evaluations of these techniques have relied on inconsistent transformations and datasets. The evaluation of five prominent watermarking methods—MaskWM, WAM, OmniGuard, TrustMark, and PixelSeal—reveals that while MaskWM offers the strongest payload recovery and localization, all tested methods remain vulnerable to specific transformations like generative inpainting and geometric misalignment.

items.title: FlexEE: Self-Speculative and KV-Compatible Early Exiting for Offloading-Aware LLM Inference
items.one_liner: FlexEE accelerates offloaded LLM inference by combining self-speculative early exiting with KV-cache-compatible hidden state management.
items.summary: Large language model inference is frequently bottlenecked by computation and memory overhead, particularly in weight-offloading scenarios where parameters move across memory hierarchies during decoding. To mitigate this latency, researchers have developed FlexEE, an early exiting framework designed for resource-constrained, offloading-based deployments. FlexEE combines layer-wise exit supervision, self-speculative decoding over a Top-K local vocabulary, and dynamic hidden state management to preserve KV-cache correctness while dropping unnecessary layers. Benchmarks demonstrate that FlexEE achieves end-to-end speedups of up to 1.27x and 3.16x on Llama2-7B and Llama3-8B under varying weight offloading conditions with minimal accuracy degradation.
items.bottom_line: FlexEE reduces offloading-induced latency during LLM inference by safely skipping execution layers via self-speculative early exits.

items.title: FirmCORe: A Benchmark for Structured Reasoning about Inter-Firm Collaboration Opportunities
items.one_liner: FirmCORe reveals that while LLMs can easily detect broad business partnerships, they frequently fail at parsing complex inter-firm operational roles.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced FirmCORe, a human-annotated benchmark comprising 2,805 labeled firm pairs designed to evaluate LLM reasoning on inter-firm collaboration opportunities. Because company data is often fragmented or private, the benchmark tests models on whether profiles indicate collaboration potential, alongside predicting partnership strength, collaboration type, and role direction. Evaluations revealed that top models achieve a macro-F1 score of 74.51 for broad opportunity detection, but score only 61.57% on exact matches across all four fields. The findings demonstrate that current LLMs excel at spotting generic partnerships but struggle with specific operational role assignments.
items.bottom_line: Current Large Language Models are reliable at identifying general inter-firm collaboration opportunities but struggle with pinpointing specific partnership types and roles.

items.title: Stream Assembly Is an Uncontrolled Treatment in Streaming Intrusion-Detection Benchmarks
items.one_liner: Stream assembly methods in intrusion-detection benchmarks act as an uncontrolled variable that can distort performance metrics and reverse model rankings.
items.summary: Streaming intrusion-detection studies typically assemble evaluation streams from network captures by replaying records round-robin, interleaving capture days, or pooling captures. Research on CICIDS2017 and LITNET-2020 demonstrates that this stream assembly process acts as an uncontrolled experimental treatment that fundamentally alters evaluation results. Specifically, reordering an identical record set under a fixed split yields held-out samples sharing only a fraction of records and can completely reverse the performance ranking of deterministic scoring models. Furthermore, pooling temporally disjoint captures generates aggregate operating points and hazard rates that distort true performance metrics, proving that published intrusion detection scores are not directly comparable across studies.
items.bottom_line: Benchmark stream assembly significantly skews intrusion detection metrics, meaning published scores across different studies cannot be reliably compared.

claims.text: We show on two benchmarks that this assembly is an uncontrolled experimental treatment changing what the evaluation measures.
claims.support_span: We show on two benchmarks that this assembly is an uncontrolled experimental treatment changing what the evaluation measures.

items.title: AquiLLM: Evaluating Faithfulness in Open-Weight RAG-LLM Systems for Scientific Research
items.one_liner: An expert evaluation of the open-weight AquiLLM platform shows strong retrieval performance in astronomy tasks, but highlights faithfulness drops during complex synthesis.
items.summary: Scientific research increasingly relies on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems as natural language interfaces for document search and analysis code generation. This study presents a domain-expert evaluation of AquiLLM, an offline RAG-LLM platform designed for astronomy research groups, evaluating faithfulness across retrieval and analysis tasks. items.bottom_line: Open-weight RAG systems reliably handle direct retrieval tasks in scientific research, but struggle with complex synthesis and ambiguity resolution without domain-expert oversight.

items.title: ReDraft, Don't Just Distill: Reference-Driven Revision for Continual VLLM Post-Training
items.one_liner: ReDraft improves multimodal model post-training by forcing models to revise their own failed rollouts using expert references, sharply reducing catastrophic forgetting.
items.summary: Continual post-training of large multimodal models often forces a trade-off between acquiring new tasks and retaining pre-trained capabilities. Supervised fine-tuning provides clear target supervision but uses off-policy objectives that induce catastrophic forgetting, while on-policy methods struggle due to sparse signals on unmastered tasks. Researchers introduce ReDraft (Reference-Driven Revision and Fine-Tuning), which mitigates this by having the model revise its own incorrect output using an expert response merely as a reference, keeping the revision only if verified. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL models demonstrate that ReDraft significantly increases target task performance while dramatically cutting prior-task forgetting compared to traditional fine-tuning.
items.bottom_line: Reference-driven revision during continual post-training allows multimodal models to master new tasks while avoiding catastrophic forgetting of prior capabilities.

items.one_liner: MarkSec unifies LLM watermark evaluation, proving that high-performing scrubbing attacks often fail quality-constrained text criteria.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed MarkSec, a general evaluation framework designed to unify the analysis of stealing, scrubbing, and spoofing attacks against LLM watermarks. items.title: Skill-based Agentic Evaluation for Real-time Data Science Tasks

items.title: Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents
items.one_liner: tlm-DRE improves multi-turn LLM agent alignment by assigning turn-specific weights and asymmetric token-level training.

items.title: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
items.one_liner: Deploy EchoPath to convert GUI agent trajectories into repeatable, parameter-controlled callable memories that drastically cut token costs.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced EchoPath, a model-agnostic execution memory harness for GUI agents that converts artifact-validated interface trajectories into standardized, parameter-controlled callable procedures. items.title: little m: An AI Agent for Industrial Process Optimization
items.one_liner: "little m" is an AI agent designed to help formulate industrial process control models, backed by the new IPC-Bench dataset.
items.summary: Manufacturing consumes one-third of global energy, making optimal process control critical for efficiency. However, synthesizing mathematical models from complex industrial specifications requires bridging unstructured text and diagrams with precise mathematical syntax, posing a challenge for general-purpose LLMs. To address this, researchers introduced "little m," an AI agent that combines a domain-specific knowledge repository with LLM interaction to formulate real-world optimization problems as mathematical models. Alongside the agent, they introduced the Industrial Process Control Benchmark (IPC-Bench), a multimodal dataset of 50 canonical scenarios. Automated and human evaluations indicate that little m significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs in generating semantically correct control models.
items.bottom_line: little m outperforms general LLMs in formulating industrial process control models by combining domain knowledge with multimodal reasoning.

items.title: Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations
items.one_liner: ICML introduces a learnable memory policy for LLMs, enabling agents to dynamically adapt to user needs over long-term interactions.
items.summary: The ICML (InteraCtive Memory Learning) framework is a multi-agent system designed to replace static memory archives in LLMs with a learnable, interactive memory policy. Using a Planner and Trigger agent, the system selectively encodes and retrieves high-value information, co-evolving through continuous interaction feedback. This approach allows agents to improve response quality over long-term conversations by aligning memory management with user needs.
items.bottom_line: ICML transforms LLM memory from a passive archive into an active, learnable policy that improves response quality over time.

items.title: Position: AI Is Not Ready for Strategic Conflicts
items.one_liner: A new position paper warns against using open-ended LLM wargames for crisis planning, highlighting critical failure modes like decision laundering and role collapse.
items.summary: Language models are increasingly utilized in open-ended strategic wargames to act as simulation agents, generate scenario branches, and adjudicate ambiguous actions. However, because model outputs shape both the simulated actions and the resulting reality, relying on them for policy or crisis response introduces severe risks. This position paper identifies five major failure modes in LM-enabled wargames—including decision laundering, adjudication opacity, role collapse, escalation-through-adjudication, and failures of strategic imagination. The authors argue that these open-ended platforms should only be used as stress-testing tools rather than definitive safety cases for real-world strategic planning.
items.bottom_line: Language models cannot safely inform strategic military or political crisis response without rigorous, auditable safety cases.

claims.text: This position paper argues that no LM-enabled wargame should inform planning, doctrine, policy, or crisis response without an auditable safety case, and that the proper use of open-ended wargames today is to stress-test decision-influencing LM agents.

items.title: Breaking the 1.58-bit Barrier for Ternary LLMs
items.one_liner: BITCOS is a distribution-adaptive storage layout that exploits high zero-weights in ternary LLMs to reduce memory footprints and accelerate decode throughput.
items.summary: Ternary large language models store weights as one of three symbols (-1, 0, +1), conventionally referencing an information-theoretic cost of ~1.58 bits per weight, which often rounds up to 1.625 bits in practice using standard five-trit packing. An analysis of symbol distributions across 29 ternary LLMs reveals that zero values account for up to 51.5% of all model weights. To exploit this sparsity, researchers introduce BITCOS, a distribution-adaptive layout that combines a dense presence bitmap with a compacted sign vector. BITCOS reduces storage requirements below standard five-trit packing for 26 out of 29 models, achieving up to 1.485 bits per weight while accelerating decode throughput on CPUs and GPUs.
key_facts: Storage efficiency: down to 1.485 bits per weight
items.bottom_line: Adapting storage layouts to the high zero-density of ternary LLMs breaks the 1.58-bit efficiency barrier and boosts hardware inference throughput.

claims.text: Motivated by this finding, we introduce BITCOS, a simple distribution-adaptive layout comprised of a dense presence bitmap plus a compacted sign vector, and costs $2 - z$ bits per weight element given a zero density $z$ in the model's weights.

items.title: Do LLMs Make Neural Distinguishers Wise?
items.one_liner: Integrating large language models into neural distinguishers does not inherently improve cryptanalytic performance unless explicit XOR operation results are provided in prompts.
items.summary: Neural distinguishers represent a cryptanalytic technique used against symmetric-key cryptography by training machine learning models on specific plaintext and ciphertext differences to recover secret keys. This study explores whether integrating large language models into neural distinguishers can enhance their cryptanalytic performance against SPECK-32/64. The evaluation yields three insights: LLMs provide no observable improvement in performance compared to standard ResNet architectures; the choice of differences loses effectiveness at high rounds for both models; and the performance of LLM-based neural distinguishers can be significantly boosted by incorporating explicit XOR operation results into the prompt design.
items.bottom_line: LLM-based neural distinguishers do not outperform traditional machine learning architectures like ResNet in symmetric-key cryptanalysis without explicit bitwise prompt structuring.

claims.text: First, by comparing the results of LLM-based neural distinguishers with ResNet in the existing work, we demonstrate that LLMs provide no observable improvement in the performance of neural distinguishers.
claims.support_span: First, by comparing the results of LLM-based neural distinguishers with ResNet in the existing work, we demonstrate that LLMs provide no observable improvement in the performance of neural distinguishers.

items.title: Mapping out your unknown: A threat hunter’s guide to GitHub
items.one_liner: Datadog details threat hunting strategies and audit log quirks for detecting compromised GitHub accounts and stolen tokens.
items.summary: Datadog Security Research investigated how attackers target GitHub audit logs, source code repositories, and CI/CD pipelines using compromised credentials, personal access tokens, and OAuth apps. Attackers exploit leaked tokens, device code phishing, or malicious IDE extensions to perform initial access, discovery, credential access, and collection. The research highlights specific detection queries and audit log nuances, such as missing IP addresses on failed requests and incomplete external identity tracking in certain api.request events. Security teams can leverage these queries to hunt for anomalous repository downloads and unauthorized token access from new ASNs.

items.title: China's August retail sales miss forecast while investment slump deepens, piling pressure on Beijing
items.one_liner: China's weak August retail sales and deepening investment slump increase pressure on Beijing for fiscal intervention.
items.summary: China's economic data for August highlights persistent structural weakness, with retail sales growing by a meager 0.4% year-on-year, missing consensus forecasts, and urban fixed-asset investment shrinking by 7.2% for the first eight months. While industrial output rose by 5.2%, authorities explicitly warned of an acute domestic imbalance between strong supply and weak demand. New bank loans expanded by just 60 billion yuan, far below expectations, as government bond financing failed to offset sluggish household and corporate demand. Economists indicate that aggressive monetary rate cuts remain unlikely, raising downside risks to Beijing's annual growth target.
items.bottom_line: Weak consumer demand and a deepening property slump are dragging down China's economic growth, putting its annual target at risk.

items.title: ZDI-26-682: Linux Kernel IPv6 Neighbour Discovery Uninitialized Memory Information Disclosure Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Linux kernel CVE-2026-43040 exposes uninitialized IPv6 Neighbour Discovery memory to privileged local attackers.
items.summary: A local information disclosure vulnerability, tracked as ZDI-26-682 and CVE-2026-43040, has been uncovered in the Linux kernel's IPv6 Neighbour Discovery implementation. The flaw arises from a lack of proper memory initialization prior to accessing userland options, allowing uninitialized kernel memory contents to be exposed. Exploiting this issue requires local attackers to already possess high-privileged code execution capabilities on the host system. Linux maintainers have issued kernel updates to patch the uninitialized memory exposure.
key_facts: Component: Linux Kernel IPv6 Neighbour Discovery
items.bottom_line: Systems running vulnerable Linux kernels must apply vendor patches to close the IPv6 Neighbour Discovery information disclosure vulnerability.

items.summary: The fraud ecosystem is shifting from large, centralized marketplaces to a fragmented landscape of specialized shops on social media and the dark web. These platforms offer 'Fraud-as-a-Service' (FaaS), providing novice criminals with infrastructure, stolen credentials, and instructional guides for schemes like business email compromise (BEC). items.title: From Bing Search to Ransomware: Bumblebee and AdaptixC2 Deliver Akira
items.one_liner: SEO poisoning remains a potent initial access vector for ransomware groups, leading to full domain compromise and massive data exfiltration.
items.summary: A sophisticated intrusion campaign beginning in July 2025 used SEO poisoning to deliver Bumblebee malware via a trojanized ManageEngine OpManager installer. The campaign concluded with the deployment of Akira ransomware across the target's infrastructure, including both root and child domains.
items.bottom_line: Defenders must monitor for trojanized installers delivered via search results and implement strict egress filtering to prevent data exfiltration via tools like FileZilla.
